title: The enduring role of contracts for difference in risk management and market creation for renewables
authors: Philipp Beiter, Jérôme Guillet, Lena Kitzing, et al.
oneLineThesis: Contracts for difference remain a durable, low-cost instrument for managing investment risk and creating markets for renewables, and will stay central to renewable deployment even as power markets mature.

title: Policy credibility is a key component for an effective and efficient EU Emissions Trading System
oneLineThesis: The effectiveness and efficiency of the EU Emissions Trading System hinge less on instrument mechanics than on the long-run credibility of the policy commitment behind it.

title: The expansion of natural gas infrastructure puts energy transitions at risk
authors: Claudia Kemfert, Fabian Präger, Hanna Brauers, et al.
oneLineThesis: Continued build-out of natural gas infrastructure creates stranded-asset and carbon-lock-in risks that undermine, rather than bridge, the clean energy transition.

title: Rapid fuel switching from coal to natural gas through effective carbon pricing
authors: I. A. Grant Wilson, Iain Staffell
oneLineThesis: A sufficiently high and credible carbon price can drive rapid coal-to-gas fuel switching in power systems, delivering near-term emissions cuts faster than capacity build-out alone.

title: Scientific discovery in the age of artificial intelligence
authors: Hanchen Wang, Tianfan Fu, Yuanqi Du, Wenhao Gao, Kexin Huang, Ziming Liu, Payal Chandak, Shengchao Liu, Peter Van Katwyk, Andreea Deac, Anima Anandkumar, Karianne Bergen, Carla P. Gomes, Shirley Ho, Pushmeet Kohli, Joan Lasenby, Jure Leskovec, Tie-Yan Liu, Arjun Manrai, Debora Marks, Bharath Ramsundar, Le Song, Jimeng Sun, Jian Tang, Petar Velickovic, Max Welling, Linfeng Zhang, Connor W. Coley, Yoshua Bengio, Marinka Zitnik
oneLineThesis: AI (self-supervised, geometric and generative deep learning) is becoming a general engine of scientific discovery across domains, reshaping how hypotheses are generated, experiments designed, and large datasets interpreted. [Article-type note: labelled a Review Article in Nature v620, but functions as the field-defining forward-looking overview of AI-for-science.]

title: Deep learning and process understanding for data-driven Earth system science
authors: Markus Reichstein, Gustau Camps-Valls, Bjorn Stevens, Martin Jung, Joachim Denzler, Nuno Carvalhais, Prabhat
oneLineThesis: Hybrid modelling that fuses deep learning with physical process understanding is the path forward for data-driven Earth-system science, including climate and the energy-relevant geophysical predictions underpinning renewables. [Confirmed Perspective, Nature v566; foundational for AI weather/climate-energy work.]
